questions: On the slalom, do line_loss_events fall below 1.0 and does max_error drop below 0.06 m?
Does the 0.10 m wheel_track give any slalom finishes, and at what completion_time?
Did steering_oscillation rise above about 0.35 on the s-bend or slalom from the extra turn authority?
Did the oval and s-bend finish rates recover to iteration 1 levels (16/20 on the s-bend)?
feedback_request.requested_changes_if_any: If line loss on the slalom falls but no trial finishes, say so, and I will consider the controller-side turn authority or a narrower span. If the oval loses finishes at 0.10 m wheel_track, report the off-track point, and I will return to 0.12 m.

intent: Restore the iteration 1 sensing (lead 0.06 m, 12 mm footprints, ±0.03 m span at 0.01 m pitch) and narrow the drive track from 0.12 m to 0.10 m for more turn authority at the slalom. Body, wheel radius and mass are unchanged. Expected: slalom line-loss events fall and the first slalom finishes appear, while the oval and s-bend recover toward their iteration 1 finish rates.
learning: Iteration 3 showed that lead 0.04 m makes the robot worse across all tracks (oval and s-bend finishes both fell), so the lead should stay at 0.06 m. The slalom line loss persisted at both leads, so lead is not the limit. The next test is wheel_track, which changes turn authority for the slalom.
rationale: Iteration 3 tested the lead reduction from 0.06 m to 0.04 m, and it made the robot worse. The oval fell from 20/20 to 14/20 finishes, the s-bend fell from 16/20 to 6/20, and the slalom stayed at 0/20 with 1.05 line-loss events and max_error 0.0643. The s-bend steering_oscillation was 0.326, below the 0.35 threshold, so the span-narrowing branch is not triggered. The slalom still loses the line before its exit with lead 0.04 m, which is the condition in the Integrator's pre-written rule. Under that rule, lead is not the main limit. Lead 0.04 m also clearly hurts the s-bend, so I revert the lead to 0.06 m, the best-measured value (iteration 1: 16/20 s-bend finishes). I keep the 12 mm footprint and the proven ±0.03 m, 7-sensor, 0.01 m pitch span. I then apply the Integrator's second rule: reduce wheel_track from 0.12 m to 0.10 m. Turn rate equals the wheel speed difference divided by wheel_track, so a narrower track gives more turn authority at the slalom's direction changes for the same PWM difference. The oval finishes in about 1.84 s and the s-bend in about 2.28 s, both under the 3 s limit, so the time margin can absorb a small loss of straight-line speed. Expected result: slalom line_loss_events fall below 1.0 and max_error drops under 0.06, with the first slalom finishes possible. The s-bend and oval should recover to the iteration 1 level, since the lead is restored. The main risk is more oscillation from higher turn authority, so the next race will report steering_oscillation on all three tracks.
